h1: Questions operators ask, answered directly.

meta.description: What is srelens? How is it different from Lens or Freelens? Where do cluster credentials go? How does the MCP integration work? Every common question about the Rust-based Kubernetes desktop client, answered.
meta.og:title: srelens FAQ — questions operators ask
meta.og:description: Platforms, credentials, kubectl, MCP, and how srelens compares to Lens and Freelens — answered directly.
meta.og:image:alt: srelens exec terminal inside a pod on a live cluster.
meta.twitter:title: srelens FAQ — questions operators ask
meta.twitter:description: Platforms, credentials, kubectl, MCP, and how srelens compares to Lens and Freelens — answered directly.

acceptedAnswer.text: srelens is a Kubernetes desktop workspace — a native GUI app for browsing, inspecting, and operating Kubernetes clusters. It reads the contexts in your local kubeconfig and gives you resource browsing across 40+ kinds, live watches, log streaming, in-pod terminals, port forwarding, Helm release views, and a schema-aware YAML editor, all in one window. It is built on Tauri v2 with a pure-Rust core.

mainEntity.name: How is srelens different from Lens or Freelens?

acceptedAnswer.text: srelens uses Tauri v2 with a pure-Rust core and connects directly to Kubernetes API servers through kube-rs. It follows a familiar Kubernetes desktop workflow while providing local-first operation and MCP access for supported backend capabilities. srelens is independently developed and is not affiliated with Mirantis Lens or the Freelens project.

mainEntity.name: What platforms does srelens run on?

acceptedAnswer.text: srelens targets macOS, Windows, and Linux desktops via Tauri v2.

No. srelens complements kubectl by giving engineers a visual workspace for investigation, analysis, and day-to-day cluster operations. The built-in local terminal still lets you use kubectl and other command-line tools when needed.

mainEntity.name: How does the AI (MCP) integration work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supported backend capabilities in srelens are registered in a shared capability registry and exposed through the built-in MCP server. MCP-capable clients can connect over stdio or loopback HTTP. Mutating tools require an explicit _confirm: true argument before they run. Additional MCP security and audit controls are planned.

mainEntity.name: Where do my cluster credentials go?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nowhere. srelens runs entirely on your machine and connects to clusters directly using the credentials in your local kubeconfig files. There is no intermediary cloud service between the app and your API servers.
Yes. Installers for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows, and Linux are published on GitHub Releases. The latest build is always available there, and you can also build srelens from source.

mainEntity.name: Are the screenshots on srelens.com real?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every product image on srelens.com is an unedited capture of srelens connected to a live three-node kind Kubernetes cluster (one control-plane and two workers) running real workloads, in both the dark and light themes of the app.
Yes. srelens is open source under the MIT license and free to download. There is no account, license key, or paid tier.

headings: The fastest answer is trying it.
